observations.note: The subject repairs CLAUDE-G20LJ-V10-S-1 by attribution rather than by carrying $.leftoverDesignClosedIfAcceptedAndRecorded as a real key. The frozen review offered both and left the choice to the author, so this is compliant. Recording only: the g21 leftover-join lineage carries the field as a top-level key across v5–v14, so the two lineages will continue to differ in shape on this point. Nothing in this artifact is defective for it.

Two instances of the deictic 'this successor' remain, at $.basedOn.predecessorV9.role and $.doesNot[29], both in the sentence 'Does not record g20 leftover-join.v9 as current after this successor is recorded.' This was considered as a possible S-2-class finding and declined. The phrase is present once in dual-ACCEPT g20 leftover-join.v9 and twice in g20 leftover-join.v10, where neither reviewer charged it while Claude did charge a different deictic in the same artifact — so the lineage has twice tested and accepted it. It is also unambiguous in place: the sentence names g20 leftover-join.v9 explicitly and contrasts it against 'this successor', which can only be the speaker. Not a finding.

The closing 'Not this artifact's version number.' on the predecessor role leaves is likewise a deictic, and is likewise long-established lineage convention carried through dual-ACCEPT g20 leftover-join.v9. It is a disambiguator against cross-lineage version confusion rather than a speaker self-reference, and reads correctly. Not a finding.

The v10 and v11 dispatches share HEAD 2b75376b, last heading D-327, required-now 28 and the same file 08 digest. The remasurement is therefore a pure findings-landing successor with no environment movement to absorb, which is why the leaf diff is as small as it is. That is the expected shape for this successor and is recorded here so a later reader does not mistake the small diff for an incomplete remasurement.

Charging 'Not this artifact's version number.' as a deictic — declined; see OBS-3.
